transcript.text: Hi everyone! Thanks for being here. We've got 30 kilograms of apples from the backyard orchard to sort this weekend into three categories: family use, community pantry donation, and freezer storage. We've got clean one-kilo boxes, freezer containers, labels, and a kitchen scale ready to go. Before I make the final call on the split, let's go around the table like we usually do — each of you, please share any practical details or considerations you think should shape the plan. Who'd like to start?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I spoke with Grandma yesterday, and she specifically asked for exactly 6 kilograms of the apples to be peeled and cooked into unsweetened applesauce, because chewing whole apples is difficult for her. I wanted to make sure the group knows this before we decide on the split.
transcript.speaker: A2

I wanted to make sure the group knows this before we decide on the split."}

transcript.text: I heard back from the community pantry coordinator — they confirmed they can accept exactly 12 kilograms of whole apples, packed as twelve labeled one-kilogram boxes, with delivery on Sunday at 10:00. So we have a firm commitment on that end if we decide to go with that amount.
transcript.speaker: A3
transcript.raw_output: {"type":"reveal","fact_id":"PF2","text":"I heard back from the community pantry coordinator — they confirmed they can accept exactly 12 kilograms of whole apples, packed as twelve labeled one-kilogram boxes, with delivery on Sunday at 10:00. So we have a firm commitment on that end if we decide to go with that amount."}

transcript.text: I should mention something useful before we finalize the plan. I received a recommendation from the county extension food-preservation adviser that the remaining 12 kilograms — after accounting for Grandma's applesauce request and the community pantry donation — should be made into unsweetened applesauce and frozen in twenty-four 500-gram containers rather than stored fresh. The adviser's view is that unsweetened applesauce freezes better and retains more nutritional value than storing whole apples in the freezer. So if we go with 6 kilos for Grandma and 12 for the pantry, that leaves exactly 12 kilos, which aligns perfectly with this recommendation.
